tasks.gr9-apartheid-system-1948-t3: Topic: The Apartheid System 1948. Cover the 1948 election victory of the National Party and the introduction of institutionalized apartheid, the Population Registration Act (1950) classifying all people by race, the Group Areas Act forcing racial residential separation, pass books restricting Black movement and employment, Bantu Education providing inferior schooling to Black children, daily dehumanization and injustice under apartheid, and the beginning of organized resistance through the ANC and other organizations. Ask Grade 9 learners to define apartheid as a system, explain key apartheid laws and their effects, describe daily life under racial oppression, analyze how apartheid used laws to entrench inequality, and evaluate the strategies available for opposing such oppression.
tasks.gr9-sophiatown-bantustans-t3: Topic: Sophiatown and Bantustans. Cover Sophiatown as a vibrant multiracial neighbourhood in Johannesburg that contradicted apartheid ideology, the forcible removal of residents and destruction of homes to make Sophiatown a white suburb, the creation of Bantustans or 'homeland' territories as impoverished reserves where Black people were forcibly relocated, how Bantustans served apartheid control by denying Black people South African citizenship, resistance to forced removals through marches and stay-aways, and the symbolic and real impact of these removals on communities. Ask Grade 9 learners to explain why Sophiatown was targeted, describe forced removals and their impact, analyze the Bantustan system as a strategy of separation and control, and discuss resistance to displacement.
tasks.gr9-defiance-campaign-freedom-charter-t3: Topic: Defiance Campaign and Freedom Charter. Cover the 1952 Defiance Campaign of non-violent civil disobedience where protesters deliberately broke unjust laws to expose their immorality, the Congress of the People in 1955 and adoption of the Freedom Charter proclaiming 'South Africa belongs to all who live in it,' key anti-apartheid leaders including Nelson Mandela, Oliver Tambo, Albert Luthuli, and others, the combination of peaceful protest with readiness for armed struggle, international support for the anti-apartheid cause growing through the 1950s. Ask Grade 9 learners to explain civil disobedience, analyze the Freedom Charter's vision, identify anti-apartheid leaders and their contributions, evaluate the effectiveness of non-violent resistance, and trace growing international pressure against apartheid.
tasks.gr9-womens-march-resistance-t3: Topic: Women's March and Resistance. Cover the Women's March of August 9, 1956, when approximately 20,000 women of all races protested pass laws, women's crucial but often overlooked leadership in anti-apartheid resistance, leaders like Winnie Madikizela-Mandela and countless others who organized and endured suffering, women bearing the double burden of apartheid in family and economic life, the transition by the 1960s from mass peaceful protest to underground and armed struggle as the apartheid state increased repression, and oral history as a means of preserving stories of those who lived through apartheid. Ask Grade 9 learners to explain the significance of the Women's March, describe women's leadership roles, analyze the barriers women faced in resistance, explain why peaceful protest gave way to armed struggle, and discuss the importance of oral history in documenting resistance.
tasks.gr9-udhr-t3: Topic: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights for Grade 9 History (CAPS term 3). Cover why it was written after World War II, the United Nations, the commission led by Eleanor Roosevelt, adoption on 10 December 1948, its 30 articles and some rights in everyday words (equality, life and liberty, movement, education, no discrimination by race), that it is a statement of standards and not a binding law, the 1948 vote (48 for, none against, 8 abstentions, including South Africa), how apartheid went against it, and the Bill of Rights in the 1996 Constitution. Ask factual and source-skills questions.
tasks.gr9-racism-myth-of-race-t3: Topic: Racism and the myth of race for Grade 9 History (CAPS term 3). Cover the definition of racism (prejudice and discrimination based on the idea of race, built into laws under apartheid), human evolution and our common ancestry (all people descended from ancestors who lived in Africa; the CAPS says as recently as 100 000 years ago, and scientists find even earlier dates), why scientists say race is a social construct and not a biological fact (the myth of race), and apartheid and the myth of race (the Population Registration Act of 1950 classified every South African into a population group using arbitrary criteria). Present the science as the CAPS does, avoid any graphic or demeaning detail, and use no contested figures. Ask factual and source-skills questions.
tasks.gr9-oral-history-project-t3: Topic: The oral history and research project for Grade 9 History (CAPS term 3). Cover what oral history is (spoken memories as a primary source, its strengths and limits), what the CAPS project asks (research an apartheid law in at least 300 words with 2 illustrations and captions, interview a person affected by it, write about 10 questions in advance, write a coherent story of 600 words, hand in the questions and answers, the story and your reflections), open and closed questions, and interviewing with care (permission, listening, notes, letting the person skip a painful question, thanking them). Ask factual and skills questions.
